Plan: Epiq Solutions Sidekiq as a wvt live device¶

Issue: #4. Branch: 4-sidekiq (from main). Status: receive implemented on 4-sidekiq (2026-10-23) against SDK 4.26.0, tested with a simulated card, and built and linked against the real SDK on Linux x86-64 and ARM64 (§9). Not yet run against a card. Transmit (Phase 7) is not done. Sections 1 to 8 are the plan; §9 records the implementation and its differences from the plan. Roadmap: version 1.3, “Support for EPIQ SDRs”.

1. Goal¶

Add Epiq Solutions Sidekiq cards to the live device list, next to RTL-SDR, USRP B2xx and BB60. The user can do these tasks:

  • Select a Sidekiq card in the Device list, or with --device skiq.

  • Tune the card, and set the sample rate, bandwidth, gain and RF port.

  • View the spectrum and waterfall.

  • Record SigMF or raw IQ.

A later phase adds transmit from the signal generator (§5, Phase 7).

Out of scope:

  • Multi-channel receive (A1 + A2 together) and phase-coherent modes.

  • 1PPS and GPS timing, and timed start.

  • FPGA bitstream changes and user FPGA applications.

  • Running wvt on the embedded Sidekiq products (Z2, Z3u, Z4, Matchstiq). wvt is an X11 desktop program. These products run their own embedded Linux.

2. API choice¶

Use libsidekiq directly. It is the Epiq SDK library, with the header sidekiq_api.h.

Option

Result

libsidekiq (chosen)

Same pattern as bb_api for the BB60: a vendor SDK, linked through CMake. Full control of block size, timestamps, overload flags and gain index. No new dependency other than the SDK

SoapySidekiq through SoapySDR

Adds SoapySDR as a dependency only for one device family. The gain mapping and timestamp checks are in the module, not in wvt. Useful as a reference for the API calls

gr-sidekiq

Needs GNU Radio. Not applicable

The SDK is not open source. Epiq gives it to customers through its support portal. wvt cannot include it in the repository or download it in CMake. The user must install it, as with the Signal Hound SDK.

Verified API facts¶

These facts come from SoapySidekiq (github.com/epiqsolutions/SoapySidekiq). That module calls libsidekiq and needs SDK 4.26.0 or later.

Topic

API

Find cards

skiq_get_cards(skiq_xport_type_auto, &count, cards) without skiq_init

Open

skiq_init(skiq_xport_type_auto, skiq_xport_init_level_full, &card, 1), then skiq_exit()

Card is in use

skiq_is_card_avail(card, &pid) gives the process that holds the card

Identity

skiq_read_serial_string, skiq_read_parameters → card_param.part_type, skiq_part_string

Sample rate

skiq_write_rx_sample_rate_and_bandwidth(card, hdl, rate, bw), skiq_read_min_sample_rate, skiq_read_max_sample_rate

Tuning

skiq_write_rx_LO_freq(card, hdl, hz)

Gain

skiq_write_rx_gain_mode (skiq_rx_gain_auto / skiq_rx_gain_manual), skiq_read_rx_gain_index_range, skiq_write_rx_gain(card, hdl, index)

I/Q order

skiq_write_iq_order_mode(card, skiq_iq_order_iq). The default order is Q then I

Resolution

skiq_read_rx_iq_resolution(card, &bits). Each card type can be different

Blocking receive

skiq_set_rx_transfer_timeout(card, 100000) (µs) makes skiq_receive block

Receive

skiq_receive(card, &hdl, &block, &len) → skiq_rx_status_success, skiq_rx_status_no_data or skiq_rx_status_error_overrun

Block layout

SKIQ_RX_HEADER_SIZE_IN_BYTES header, then interleaved int16 I/Q in block->data. The header has rf_timestamp and sys_timestamp

Lost samples

rf_timestamp of a block must equal the previous one plus the samples per block

Block size

skiq_read_rx_block_size(card, skiq_rx_stream_mode_balanced)

Start / stop

skiq_start_rx_streaming(card, hdl), skiq_stop_rx_streaming(card, hdl)

Other

skiq_write_rx_rf_port_for_hdl, skiq_rf_port_string, skiq_write_ref_clock_select, skiq_read_rx_overload_state, skiq_read_rx_cal_offset, skiq_register_logging

Gain index mapping in SoapySidekiq (one step = one index):

Part types

dB per step

dB = 0 at index

mPCIe, M.2, M.2-2280 (Stretch), Z2, Z3u

1

0

X2, X4, X40

0.5

195

NV100, NVM2, Z4

0.5

187

wvt always clamps the index to the range from skiq_read_rx_gain_index_range.

To check against the SDK manual¶

The SDK manual is in the SDK download. These items are not in SoapySidekiq, or they can be different between SDK versions. §9.1 gives the answers from SDK 4.26.0:

  • Does skiq_set_rx_transfer_timeout work on the USB transport? If not, the receive thread must poll and sleep for a short time.

  • Can wvt call skiq_write_rx_LO_freq and skiq_write_rx_gain while the card streams?

  • Does skiq_write_ref_clock_select apply at once, or only after a new skiq_init?

  • Does each card type support skiq_rx_gain_auto?

  • Does an SDK older than 4.26 supply bin/sidekiq-config? If not, CMake needs a second way to find the library (§3, Build).

  • Do 12-bit cards put the sample in the low 12 bits (sign-extended) or in the high 12 bits? The scaling in §3 depends on this. A test with a known input level gives the answer.

3. Design decisions¶

Topic

Decision

Reason

Driver id

"skiq". Device args = serial number, or #N for card number N

Short. The serial number stays the same when the PCIe order changes

Target cards

Cards attached to an x86-64 Linux host: M.2, M.2-2280 (Stretch), NV100, X2, X4. mPCIe if available

wvt runs on a desktop. The embedded products are out of scope

Transport

skiq_xport_type_auto. PCIe gives full rate. USB (mPCIe and M.2) gives a low rate. Show the transport in the device description

One code path. The user sees why a rate is not possible

Handle

skiq_rx_hdl_A1 only

Single-channel view. Multi-channel is out of scope

Build switch

WVT_WITH_SKIQ = AUTO / ON / OFF. Find the SDK with -DSIDEKIQ_SDK_DIR=..., then env SIDEKIQ_SDK_DIR, then ~/sidekiq_sdk_current

Same pattern as WVT_WITH_BB. Same search order as SoapySidekiq

Library lookup

Run bin/sidekiq-config --cflags --libs-static. Keep the static link flags in their order on an imported target

The SDK has no pkg-config file. The link order of the static libraries is important

Sample format

SampleFormat::CI16. Set skiq_iq_order_iq so the data is I then Q, as in a ci16 file

The ring, the recorder and SigMF already handle ci16 (USRP, BB60)

Scaling

Shift each sample left by 16 - resolution bits in the receive thread. A full-scale signal then reads 0 dBFS on 12-bit and 16-bit cards

wvt decodes ci16 as value / 32768. Without the shift, a 12-bit card reads 24 dB low

Gain

StreamConfig::gain in dB. The backend maps dB to a gain index per part type (table in §2). GainRange shows the dB range of the card

The user sets dB, as for the other drivers

AGC

StreamConfig::agc → skiq_rx_gain_auto if the card supports it. Else the Auto box is not shown

Same control as RTL-SDR and USRP

Bandwidth

StreamConfig::bandwidth. 0 = 80 % of the sample rate

Same field as USRP and BB60

RF port

StreamConfig::antenna holds the port name from skiq_rf_port_string. Empty = card default

Reuse the USRP antenna field and combo

External reference

StreamConfig::extRef → skiq_write_ref_clock_select(external)

Same flag as the BB60

Receive thread

One thread. skiq_receive with a 100 ms timeout. Copy and shift each block into a buffer of about 20 ms, then call data_

Same block size as the BB60 backend. Fewer ring writes

Lost samples

Check rf_timestamp continuity. A gap of N samples calls gap_(N, "sample loss"). skiq_rx_status_error_overrun calls gap_(-1, "overrun")

The ring and the recorder already count gaps

Overload

Read the overload state about 2 times per second. Show “ADC overload” in notes() for 1 s

Same as the BB60 backend

Retune

Write the LO frequency while the card streams, if the SDK allows it (§2). Else stop, write, start, and purge

The UI already starts a new capture segment on retune

SDK messages

skiq_register_logging writes SDK messages to stderr with a wvt: skiq: prefix. Errors also go to notes()

The SDK writes to stdout by default. That mixes with --list-devices output

Card in use

Before skiq_init, call skiq_is_card_avail. If another process holds the card, give its PID in the error

A clear message instead of a timeout

4. Rates and limits¶

The backend reads the limits from the card after skiq_init. It does not use a fixed table. checkSampleRate("skiq") only checks that the rate is positive and not more than 250 MS/s. After open, the backend compares the rate with skiq_read_min_sample_rate and skiq_read_max_sample_rate, and gives an error that names the card’s range.

Expected limits (to check on hardware):

Card

RF chip

Resolution

Typical maximum rate

M.2, mPCIe, M.2-2280

AD9361 / AD9364

12 bits

61.44 MS/s on PCIe, much less on USB

X2

ADRV9009

16 bits

245.76 MS/s

X4

2 × ADRV9009

16 bits

245.76 MS/s per channel

NV100

ADRV9002

16 bits

about 61.44 MS/s

Rates above 20 MS/s need the GPU build for “FFT sees 100%” in live mode (see docs/design/cuda-gpu-plan.md). Rates above 100 MS/s are more than the GPU path analyzes. The recorder must write at 4 bytes × rate. At 245.76 MS/s, that is about 1 GB/s. The README must tell the user to record to a fast NVMe disk, or to use a lower rate.

5. Work breakdown¶

Phase 0 — SDK and hardware access¶

  • [x] Get the Sidekiq SDK (4.26.0 or later if possible) from the Epiq support portal. Record the SDK version and the card types that are available for tests.

  • [ ] Install the kernel modules and udev rules from the SDK. Check with the SDK test application rx_samples that a card streams.

  • [x] Answer the items in §2, “To check against the SDK manual”. Update this plan (§9.1).

Phase 1 — Build system (CMakeLists.txt)¶

  • [x] WVT_WITH_SKIQ (AUTO / ON / OFF) and SIDEKIQ_SDK_DIR cache variables.

  • [x] Find bin/sidekiq-config in the order from §3. Run it for --cflags, --libs-static and --version. Make an INTERFACE IMPORTED target sidekiq that keeps the link flags in their order.

  • [x] If found: add src/device/sdr_skiq.cpp, define WVT_HAVE_SKIQ, and print wvt: Sidekiq support enabled (SDK x.y.z). If not found: ON is a fatal error. AUTO prints a status line.

  • [x] Skip on macOS with a status line. The SDK is for Linux only.

  • [x] If an older SDK has no sidekiq-config, add a second lookup: sidekiq_api.h and libsidekiq__<arch>.a with the support libraries that the SDK manual lists.

Phase 2 — Device abstraction (src/device/sdr_device.h, src/device/sdr_device.cpp)¶

  • [x] Comments for the skiq use of args, gain, bandwidth, antenna and extRef.

  • [x] sdrDrivers(), enumerateDevices() with a “Sidekiq (none detected)” entry, and openDevice() dispatch.

  • [x] checkSampleRate("skiq"): positive and ≤ 250 MS/s. A warning above 61.44 MS/s about disk speed for recording.

  • [x] GainRange: add std::vector<std::string> ports if the RF port combo needs a list from the device. Else use a new SdrDevice::rfPorts() method. Choose the smaller change.

Phase 3 — Backend (src/device/sdr_skiq.cpp, new)¶

  • [x] enumerateSkiq(): skiq_get_cards, then for each card the serial number and part type. The label is, for example, Sidekiq X4 serial 8N3H (PCIe).

  • [x] Open: find the card by serial number or #N. Check skiq_is_card_avail. Call skiq_init. Read the part type, resolution, rate range and gain index range.

  • [x] Configure: I/Q order, reference clock, RF port, rate and bandwidth, LO frequency, gain mode and gain index. Read back the actual rate with skiq_read_rx_sample_rate_and_bandwidth.

  • [x] Receive thread:

    • Get the block size from skiq_read_rx_block_size.

    • Call skiq_receive with a timeout. Check the handle and the block length.

    • Shift each sample by 16 - resolution bits.

    • Check the timestamps for gaps.

  • [x] Errors: count the receive errors other than no_data and overrun. After 10 in sequence, set fatalError() and stop the thread. This occurs, for example, when the user removes the card.

  • [x] setCenterFreq, setGain (dB → index, clamp), gainRange() per part type.

  • [x] Overload poll and notes().

  • [x] stop(): skiq_stop_rx_streaming, join the thread, skiq_exit.

  • [x] Put the pure logic in functions without SDK types. These are the dB-to-index mapping, the timestamp gap check and the sample shift. Phase 6 tests them without hardware.

Phase 4 — CLI (src/app/main.cpp)¶

  • [x] --device skiq[:SERIAL|#N]. Reuse --gain, --bandwidth, --antenna (RF port) and --ext-ref.

  • [x] Default rate 10 MS/s for skiq when -r is not given.

  • [x] Help text: --device line, and “BB60 / Sidekiq” for --ext-ref.

Phase 5 — GUI (src/app/app_live.cpp)¶

  • [x] Driver name “Sidekiq”. Default gain range until a card is open.

  • [x] Rate tooltip: the card’s range after open, and the USB note.

  • [x] Gain slider in dB, Auto box only if the card supports AGC.

  • [x] RF port combo from the card’s port list (as the USRP antenna combo).

  • [x] Ext ref checkbox (as BB60). Apply on change, with a stream restart if Phase 0 shows that it is necessary.

Phase 6 — Tests and docs¶

  • [x] tools/skiq_check.cpp tests the pure logic from Phase 3 without the SDK. Every build makes it. It tests:

    • dB-to-index for each part type, with clamping.

    • Timestamp gaps: no gap, one lost block, and wrap-around of the 64-bit counter.

    • The shift for 12-bit and 16-bit cards.

  • [x] Write a manual hardware test list. It covers:

    • Each available card type, on PCIe and on USB.

    • Rates from the minimum to the maximum of each card.

    • Retune while streaming, gain steps, and the overload note.

    • A 60 s recording at the highest rate that the disk supports.

    • Removal of the card while streaming.

  • [x] README.md, in Simplified Technical English as the rest of the README:

    • A build section for the SDK.

    • Device setup: kernel modules, udev rules, and one process per card.

    • A device table column, the CLI options, the source file table and roadmap row 1.3.

Phase 7 — Optional: transmit from the signal generator¶

  • [ ] openSkiqTx for SdrTx (src/device/sdr_tx.h): skiq_tx_block_allocate, skiq_transmit, skiq_write_tx_LO_freq, skiq_write_tx_attenuation, skiq_start_tx_streaming and skiq_stop_tx_streaming.

  • [ ] Transmit gain as attenuation (the Sidekiq controls TX power with attenuation). The SdrTx gain range shows it as negative dB, or the UI shows “Attenuation”.

  • [ ] openTx dispatch, --tx-args skiq[:SERIAL], and the signal generator window (src/app/app_siggen.cpp now accepts only uhd).

  • [ ] Underrun count from skiq_read_tx_num_underruns into SdrTx::Stats.

6. Risks¶

Risk

Handling

No SDK on the development computer (macOS)

The backend compiles only on Linux with the SDK. Keep the pure logic separate and test it on every build (Phase 6)

The API is different between SDK versions

Set a minimum SDK version in CMake (4.26.0 if Phase 0 shows that it works). Print the SDK version in the status line and in description()

libsidekiq is static and has its own support libraries

Use the order from sidekiq-config --libs-static without change

Only one process can open a card

Check skiq_is_card_avail and name the other process

12-bit scaling is wrong

Phase 0 test with a known input. skiq_check tests the shift

High rates (X2 / X4) are more than the host can record or analyze

Warnings in checkSampleRate and in the README. The “FFT sees” readout already shows the analyzed part

The SDK writes to stdout

skiq_register_logging before skiq_init

skiq_exit is global for the process

Only one Sidekiq device object at a time. openDevice refuses a second open with a clear message

7. Acceptance criteria¶

  1. A build without the SDK, and every macOS build, has no change in behavior.

  2. wvt --list-devices shows each attached card with its type, serial number and transport.

  3. wvt --device skiq -c 915M -r 10M shows a live spectrum. A signal generator tone at a known level reads within 3 dB of the expected dBFS on a 12-bit and a 16-bit card.

  4. Retune and gain changes take effect in less than 200 ms with no fatal error.

  5. A 60 s SigMF recording at 10 MS/s has no sample loss. wvt opens it with the same rate, frequency and format as the recording.

  6. When the user removes a card (or the transport fails), the status bar shows the error and wvt continues to run.

  7. skiq_check passes.

8. Open questions¶

  • Which Sidekiq cards and SDK version are available for development and tests?

  • Are the cards on PCIe, USB, or both?

  • Is transmit (Phase 7) part of version 1.3, or later?

  • Is a calibrated dBm readout wanted? skiq_read_rx_cal_offset gives the offset from dBFS to dBm for the current gain. This needs a new “dBm” mode in the spectrum axis.

9. Implementation record (2026-10-23)¶

The receive path (Phases 1 to 6) is on 4-sidekiq. It was written against the SDK 4.26.0 headers and manual (sidekiq_api.h, the HTML SDK manual, the sidekiq_probe example). No card was available.

9.1 Answers from the SDK manual (4.26.0)¶

Question

Answer

What wvt does

Does skiq_set_rx_transfer_timeout work on USB?

No. Developing apps: “not all transports support blocking receive”; skiq_get_rx_transfer_timeout gives RX_TRANSFER_WAIT_NOT_SUPPORTED on USB and custom transports

A 25 ms timeout (the manual’s advice). If it fails or is not supported, the thread polls: it sleeps 0.5 ms after no_data

Retune and gain change while streaming?

Yes. skiq_init makes three mutexes per card, so the calls are thread-safe. On AD9361 cards (mPCIe, M.2, M.2-2280, Z2, Z3u) a retune or rate change stops the sample clock, and the RF timestamp slips (Timestamp Slips within AD9361 Products)

Write the LO while the card streams. No gap check for 0.5 s after a retune, so the slip is not counted as a loss

skiq_write_ref_clock_select at once or after skiq_init?

At once, but it starts a full RF initialization, so the RF settings must come after it. M.2 and mPCIe: not supported at run time (only the stored setting, with the ref_clock test app)

Write it first in configure(). On the M.2 and mPCIe, the error tells the user about ref_clock

skiq_rx_gain_auto on each card?

The API does not say which cards have it

Try skiq_write_rx_gain_mode(auto) after open. GainRange::agc = the result

bin/sidekiq-config in older SDKs?

4.26.0 has it (doc/sidekiq-config.md). Older SDKs are unknown

Use it if present. Else link lib/libsidekiq__<cpu>.a with the flags of the 4.26.0 share/sidekiq/sidekiq-config/<cpu>.conf, and read the version from LIBSIDEKIQ_VERSION_*

12-bit samples: low or high bits?

Low bits, sign-extended to 16 bits (skiq_iq_order_t in sidekiq_types.h)

Shift left by 16 - resolution (×16 on 12-bit cards), as planned

9.2 Differences from the plan¶

Topic

Plan

Implementation

Reason

Gain mapping

dB = 0 at a fixed index per part type (195 on X2/X4, 187 on NV100), from SoapySidekiq

dB above the lowest index from skiq_read_rx_gain_index_range, with the step per part type (1 dB AD9361, 0.5 dB other cards)

The API documents the step but not an absolute 0 dB index. This needs no offset table that can be wrong

Overload

Poll skiq_read_rx_overload_state 2 times per second

Also the overload bit in each block header

The header bit is per block. The manual: USB blocks have the header word set to 0, so the poll stays for USB

RF ports

GainRange::ports or SdrDevice::rfPorts()

DeviceCaps::antennas (already there for the USRP) from skiq_rx_param_t::fixed_rf_ports

No new interface. TRX ports need skiq_write_rf_port_config and an Rx/Tx operation: out of scope

Device list

skiq_get_cards, serial and part type

skiq_get_cards, skiq_is_card_avail, then skiq_init(basic) for the free cards to read part, serial and transport, then skiq_exit (as sidekiq_probe)

skiq_read_parameters needs an initialized card. A card in use is listed as #N with the PID of the owner. While wvt has a card open, the list shows that card only

SDK messages

To stderr with a wvt: skiq: prefix

To the wvt log, component skiq (errors at ERROR, warnings at WARN, the rest at DEBUG)

The log already goes to the console and the log file

Overrun

gap_(-1, "overrun")

The next block’s timestamp gives the exact count: gap_(N, "Sidekiq overrun ...")

Exact counts in the SigMF annotations

syslog.h

—

sidekiq_types.h includes <syslog.h>, whose LOG_DEBUG and LOG_INFO clash with the wvt log macros. sdr_skiq.cpp keeps the SDK levels and #undefs the two names before the wvt headers

Found when the backend was compiled against the real header

CMake search

SIDEKIQ_SDK_DIR, env, ~/sidekiq_sdk_current

Also the newest third_party/sidekiq_sdk/sidekiq_sdk_v* (git-ignored)

The SDK for this work was extracted there

Minimum SDK

4.26.0 if possible

4.14.0 (skiq_write_ref_clock_select). Only 4.26.0 is tested

Older SDKs can work; CMake prints the version

README

Build section, device setup, table, roadmap

In docs/live.md, docs/build.md, docs/cli.md, docs/self-checks.md, docs/source-layout.md. The README lists the device

The README now points to the docs pages; it has no roadmap table

9.3 Tests that ran¶

  • skiq_check in every build: the gain mapping and its clamps, the lost-sample count (with the 64-bit wrap and a timestamp that goes back), the 12-bit shift, the Q/I swap (also in place) and the rate rule.

  • skiq_check with -DWVT_SKIQ_SIM=ON (macOS arm64): the device list, open by first card, serial and #N; the errors (unknown serial, card number, rate and LO range, port name, external reference on an M.2, card in use with its PID, no card); a second open refused; real-time streaming; the tone offset after a retune; the tone level at −30 dBFS on a 12-bit M.2 and a 16-bit X4; no false gap from the simulated AD9361 timestamp slip (the test fails without the 0.5 s pause); overload note on and off; AGC; restart after stop; USB with polled receive and polled overload; an overrun counted as exactly 5090 samples; a card removal as a fatal error.

  • A 3 s headless SigMF recording from the simulated card at 5 MS/s: 60 MB, no gaps, ci16_le, the card in core:hw. A GUI screenshot under Xvfb shows the tone at −30 dBFS.

  • High rates with the simulated X4 (WVT_SKIQ_SIM_PART=x4, macOS arm64, Apple M5, internal SSD), headless SigMF: 5 s each at 122.88, 200 and 245.76 MS/s, and 20 s at 245.76 MS/s (19.66 GB, 20.3 s wall time, 0 gaps, the tone at +200 kHz and −30 dBFS at the start, middle and end of the file; about 60 % of one CPU core with the simulator). The simulator copies its signal from a table, and it reports an overrun when the host falls more than 64 MiB behind (an assumed DMA buffer size). skiq_check stalls the host for 0.5 s at 100 MS/s and checks that wvt counts the loss. This tests wvt’s path from skiq_receive to the disk, not the PCIe and DMA of a real X4.

  • A build with the real SDK 4.26.0 in Ubuntu 24.04 containers, x86-64 and ARM64, with -DWVT_WITH_SKIQ=ON -DWVT_WERROR=ON: CMake found the SDK in third_party/, sidekiq-config gave the static link flags, and wvt links and runs. With no card, --list-devices shows Sidekiq (none detected), and --device skiq gives no Sidekiq card found.

  • A macOS build without the SDK: Sidekiq support disabled (the Sidekiq SDK is for Linux only), no change in behavior.

9.4 Hardware test list (still to do)¶

For each card type that is available (M.2 and X4 first), on PCIe, and on USB for the M.2:

  1. sidekiq_probe sees the card. wvt --list-devices shows it with its part, serial number and transport.

  2. wvt --device skiq -c 915M -r 10M: a signal generator tone at a known level reads within 3 dB of the expected dBFS (acceptance criterion 3). Do this on a 12-bit and a 16-bit card: this checks the shift.

  3. Rates from the minimum to the maximum of the card. The error for a rate out of range names the card’s range. On USB, find the highest rate without gaps and add it to docs/live.md.

  4. Retune while streaming, many times: no gap is reported, the tone moves, and the change takes less than 200 ms (the log at DEBUG shows the tune time). On an X4, check if the timestamp slips; if not, the 0.5 s pause can be limited to AD9361 cards.

  5. Gain steps across the range. The dB per step matches the slider. AGC on the cards that have it.

  6. An input above 0 dBm (with care): the RF overload note shows, also on USB.

  7. RF port and external reference (X4: with a 10 MHz source; M.2: the error message).

  8. A 60 s SigMF recording at 10 MS/s: no sample loss; wvt opens it with the same rate, frequency and format (acceptance criterion 5). Then the highest rate that the disk supports.

  9. A second program (rx_samples) holds the card: wvt names its PID.

  10. Remove the card or the USB cable while streaming: the status bar shows the error, wvt keeps running (acceptance criterion 6).

9.5 Remaining work¶

  • The hardware tests in §9.4.

  • Phase 7 (transmit), if version 1.3 needs it (§8).

  • TRX RF ports (skiq_write_rf_port_config), if a user needs them.

  • A calibrated dBm readout from skiq_read_rx_cal_offset (§8).
